entry.title: Doom GPU Flame Graphs
entry.summary:
Imagine halving the resource costs of AI and what that could mean for the planet and the industry -- based on extreme estimates such savings could reduce the total US power usage by over 10% by 2030 1 . At Intel we've been creating a new analyzer tool to help reduce AI costs called AI Flame Graphs : a visualization that shows an AI accelerator or GPU hardware profile along with the full software stack, based on my CPU flame graphs . Our first version is available to customers in the Intel Tiber AI Cloud as a preview for the Intel Data Center GPU Max Series (previously called Ponte Vecchio).

Source: Brendan Gregg (Systems Performance & eBPF) · Tags: #kernel-os #performance #compilers #combinatorics

entry.title: Post-Quantum Migration of Wi-Fi Key Establishment: A Hybrid ML-KEM Design for OWE and FILS, Validated on OWE with hostapd
entry.summary:
The key agreements that protect a Wi-Fi connection rely on Diffie-Hellman, which a sufficiently capable quantum computer would break; an adversary can therefore record an association today and decrypt its traffic years later. Key establishment is thus the part of IEEE 802.11 that has to be migrated first. This work targets the two protocols that perform that agreement inside the frames used to set up the link: Opportunistic Wireless Encryption (OWE), which encrypts otherwise open networks, and Fast Initial Link Setup (FILS), designed for fast connection in dense and mobile deployments.

Source: arXiv Systems & Architecture (cs.OS, cs.AR, cs.NI, cs.PF) · Tags: #computer-architecture #kernel-os #cryptography #networking

entry.title: Package managers have an integrity problem
entry.summary:
I tested 25 of the most popular package managers to check whether they detect a compromised package repository injecting malicious code into legitimate packages. This code integrity problem could be solved using cryptographic hashes or signatures, but many package managers are still vulnerable to this threat. Of the 25 package managers reviewed 1 , fewer than half used lockfiles that checked for tampering by default, and only two verified the integrity of every package they downloaded.

Source: Trail of Bits Security Research · Tags: #infosec #cryptography #rust #databases

entry.title: Policy and Disclosure: 2026 Edition
entry.summary:
Since 2021, Project Zero has followed a “90 + 30” vulnerability disclosure policy, allowing vendors up to 90 days to remediate a vulnerability plus an extra 30 days “soak time” for patch rollout. Our goal was to encourage faster patching and give vendors time to deliver patches to users. The advent of AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and exploitation has changed the threat landscape such that the vulnerability remediation timeline encouraged by our disclosure policy is clearly insufficient.

Source: Google Project Zero · Tags: #infosec #kernel-os

entry.title: Fuzzers vs. AI: Comparing Fuzzilli and BigSleep on JavaScript Engines
entry.summary:
Summary Project Zero compared two automated tools used by Google to find vulnerabilities in Chrome’s JavaScript engine, V8, on a regular basis. Fuzzilli is a generative JavaScript engine fuzzer and BigSleep is an LLM-based bug finding system. In the past six months, BigSleep found more vulnerabilities than Fuzzilli (45 versus 37) with a 25% overlap in the specific bugs reported.

Source: Google Project Zero · Tags: #infosec #kernel-os #agents

entry.title: How to fix a bug in a fix
entry.summary:
Project Zero often works with software vendors to remediate the vulnerabilities we report and provide broader guidance on making software more secure. Some vendors express concern about potential scenarios in which they are unable to fix vulnerabilities that are causing immediate user harm, due to limitations in their patch delivery systems. Since Project Zero encounters a wide array of systems designed to protect users in the case of exceptional exploitation scenarios, both through vendor discussions and security reviews, we want to share what we’ve learned.

Source: Google Project Zero · Tags: #infosec #kernel-os
